# Jda Programming Language

> A high-performance systems language with built-in concurrency and ML — without GC. Bootstrapped from raw x86-64 assembly. The compiler compiles itself.

Jda compiles to native x86-64 Linux ELF binaries. No runtime, no GC, no libc. Self-hosted compiler written in Jda.

## Docs

- [Language Reference](https://github.com/jdalang/jda-lang/blob/main/docs/language/syntax.md): Variables, types, functions, control flow, operators
- [Structs & OOP](https://github.com/jdalang/jda-lang/blob/main/docs/language/structs.md): Structs, traits, impl, derive, generics, closures
- [Standard Library](https://github.com/jdalang/jda-lang/blob/main/docs/language/stdlib.md): 136 packages — data structures, networking, crypto, ML
- [LLM Context File](https://github.com/jdalang/jda-lang/blob/main/docs/llm-context.md): Complete language reference optimized for LLM context windows
- [Stdlib Index (JSON)](https://github.com/jdalang/jda-lang/blob/main/docs/stdlib-index.json): Machine-readable index of every stdlib package and function signature
- [Examples](https://github.com/jdalang/jda-lang/tree/main/examples): Working example programs
- [Getting Started](https://github.com/jdalang/jda-lang/tree/main/docs/getting-started): Hands-on guides

Machine-readable output: `jda check --json <file>` emits diagnostics as JSON
(stable `JDA-*` codes, `file`/`line`/`col`/`message`/`snippet`) and compiles
without writing a binary.
